reference.source: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine / Goldfrank's Toxicologic Emergencies
clinicalPearls: A systemic, multiorgan hypersensitivity reaction typically beginning within the first six weeks of starting abacavir, an antiretroviral used in HIV
Presents with a combination of fever, rash, gastrointestinal symptoms (nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain), malaise and often respiratory symptoms
The reaction is strongly and specifically associated with carriage of the HLA-B*57:01 allele
Pre-treatment HLA-B*57:01 screening is standard practice and dramatically reduces the incidence of true immunologically confirmed reactions
Symptoms characteristically worsen with each successive dose, in contrast to many self-limiting drug intolerances
Management is immediate and permanent discontinuation of abacavir with supportive care
Rechallenge after a genuine hypersensitivity reaction is contraindicated because it can precipitate rapid, life-threatening hypotension and collapse
Absence of HLA-B*57:01 makes an immunologically confirmed reaction very unlikely but does not entirely exclude other drug intolerance
reference.pathophysiology: Abacavir hypersensitivity is an HLA-restricted, T-cell-mediated immune reaction. Abacavir binds non-covalently within the antigen-binding groove of the HLA-B*57:01 molecule, altering the repertoire of self-peptides that are presented at the cell surface. This altered peptide display is recognised as foreign by cytotoxic CD8 T cells, driving a clonal T-cell response and release of inflammatory cytokines that produce the systemic multiorgan syndrome. Because the interaction is specific to the HLA-B*57:01 allele, susceptibility is genetically determined and can be predicted by pre-treatment genotyping. Repeat exposure amplifies the primed immune response, explaining the escalating severity and the danger of rechallenge.
additionalDifferentials: Intercurrent viral or opportunistic infection in an HIV-positive patient
Other drug hypersensitivity reactions (e.g. to co-administered antiretrovirals or antimicrobials)
additionalInvestigations: Full blood count and eosinophil count
Liver and renal function tests to assess organ involvement
Careful medication timeline correlating symptoms with dosing
Patch testing in specialist evaluation of uncertain historical reactions
redFlags: Hypotension or cardiovascular collapse, particularly after re-exposure
Any inadvertent rechallenge in a patient with a prior genuine reaction
reference.prognosis: With prompt and permanent withdrawal, the reaction resolves fully over days and the outlook is excellent. Continued dosing or, especially, rechallenge can cause severe hypotension and death, so lifelong avoidance is mandatory once a genuine reaction has occurred.
pitfalls: Rechallenging a patient who has had a genuine reaction, risking fatal hypotension
Failing to perform HLA-B*57:01 screening before initiating abacavir
Attributing early symptoms to a viral illness and continuing the drug
Labelling every mild intolerance as hypersensitivity, which unnecessarily removes a useful agent
references: CPIC Guideline for HLA-B and abacavir
